name: Witness

paragraphs: A Witness miner registers a hotkey, the key a miner works with, and serves a fixed video model so validators, the participants who score the miners’ work, can download and run it. You need a CPU server with a public port, normally 8091, that stays reachable during evaluation. The server needs room for the model, which is capped at 24 or 44 GB depending on architecture, but serving requires no GPU. The miner guide specifies no third-party API account for serving the model, while evaluators need API credentials for labeling and judging. Chain transactions can cost money, although Witness charges no challenge fee.

Each evaluator tests contenders on the same clips and compares their timestamped descriptions of sights, speech, text and sounds against two references, rewarding accuracy, coverage and timing. From window 30, answer speed contributes up to 10% of the clip’s quality score to its reward. To replace the winner, a challenger needs quality above 0.05 and the largest reward lead above 0.02 after weighting by evaluator stake. The winner gets all normal miner weight, while all weight burns without a registered winner or under an operator override.

Registration and submission must both happen before the opening block of a two-epoch window. From window 13, the code allows up to 30 minutes per paired attempt, including preparation, with 60 seconds per clip. Each evaluator allows 15 minutes per model for active transfer and verification across retries and windows, excluding time in the queue. The cited guides give no duration for protection from deregistration. Each hotkey binds one model apart from a one-time reset at window 32. The 100,000-alpha download threshold applies to validators, who can keep or redistribute the weights. Read from https://github.com/witnessvision/witness_subnet/ at commit 4770712 on 2026-11-23.
mining_note.how_it_was_made: This note was put together by AI agents and not by a person who mines here. One agent read the subnet's public repository and wrote down what a miner does, what it takes and how the work is paid, with a source for each statement, and a second agent opened every source and took out whatever it did not support. Of 22 source checks, 20 held, 1 did not hold and 1 could not be opened, and only what held is in the text above. Nothing of the subnet's code was run, and the note describes the code as it stood on the day and at the commit named in its last sentence, so it can be out of date.
